alt: A 3 by 3 grid sits beside a set of (row, col) tuples. Each input line names one cell. A new pair is added to the set and marked on the grid. A pair already in the set is reported as a repeat and changes nothing. The last step shows how many different cells were stored.

steps.caption: `(1, 2) in visited` is False, so `visited.add((1, 2))` stores the whole pair as one value. The grid marks row 1, column 2.
`(0, 0) in visited` is False, so `visited.add((0, 0))` stores the whole pair as one value. The grid marks row 0, column 0.
The pair (1, 2) is already in `visited`, so `(row, col) in visited` is True. The program prints "again 1 2" and adds nothing.
`(2, 1) in visited` is False, so `visited.add((2, 1))` stores the whole pair as one value. The grid marks row 2, column 1.
`len(visited)` is 3, the number of different cells stored, however many lines named them.
`(0, 0) in visited` is False, so `visited.add((0, 0))` stores the whole pair as one value. The grid marks row 0, column 0.
The pair (0, 0) is already in `visited`, so `(row, col) in visited` is True. The program prints "again 0 0" and adds nothing.
The pair (0, 0) is already in `visited`, so `(row, col) in visited` is True. The program prints "again 0 0" and adds nothing.
`len(visited)` is 1, the number of different cells stored, however many lines named them.
